note: How a control reads a written number (plan section 7.15, AD-31). One golden set for two
src-tauri/resources/scripts/_nc_machine.py (unittest). A disagreement between them is a
Every value below comes from the arithmetic of the declared parameters, not from anyone's
manual: a preset says 'a length without a point is a count of 0.001 mm', and the cases work
out what that makes of X50. The presets themselves are documented defaults of a machine
configuration, never facts about a machine (section 8, section 8.8).
'inputs' are NumberInput objects a machine may carry, 'decls' are machineParams
declarations (either a built-in profile by id, or written here where the profile ships
later), and 'profiles' are the profiles the class rules are read from.

is-b.note: the fanuc-gcode preset is-b: lengths, angles and the dwell in increments of 0.001; M9 (WP9.5a): a point-less feed per minute in 1 mm/min (0.01 in/min), per revolution in 0.01 mm/rev (0.0001 in/rev), as the control counts them without calculator-type input

is-c.note: the fanuc-gcode preset is-c: lengths, angles and the dwell one decimal finer; the point-less feeds count as on is-b, because their increment is a parameter of its own

calculator.note: the fanuc-gcode preset calculator: every position as written, with or without a point, and the micron parameters of a cycle in increments of 0.001

angles-only.note: G8 M6: a control that declares an angular increment and no dwell increment. Section 7.15 chains the dwell to the digits of incrementMm; the angular increment is not a step on that chain, and reading a dwell in it would give a wrong time with nothing said. No shipped preset looks like this, which is why nothing caught it.

okuma-1mm.note: section 8.8, the Okuma 1 mm unit system: as written (a scale whose unit is 1)

okuma-1um.note: section 8.8, the Okuma 1 um unit system: every literal is multiplied, with or without a point

okuma-10um.note: section 8.8, the Okuma 10 um unit system; the control has no 10 um inch system, so M9 (WP9.5a) gives an inch word on it no value instead of inventing a unit of 0.001 in

mixed.note: not a shipped preset: one machine that reads every class differently, so the per-class rules are covered

broken-zero.note: a hand-edited machines.json with an unusable increment: no word gets a value, none is guessed

odd-increment.note: an increment that is not a power of ten, so the write-back division does not terminate

okuma.note: the section 8.8 Okuma declaration, written here because that profile ships in M8 (P8)

class.note: M9 review F9: an incremental twin is the kind of number of the axis it moves. H of C is an angle, not a length
M9 review F9: the twin of a linear axis stays a length
1. a cycle parameter wins over everything: Q of a peck cycle is a count of least increments
1b. the same rule names a class outright: the X of a dwell block is a time, not a position
1c. a repeat count is a plain integer and is never converted
1d. the same letter, another cycle: without a unit the address decides, so K is an arc centre
1e. L as a repeat count of a cycle
2. the feed word of a block whose F is a time (Okuma and Sinumerik G4, M8) is a dwell
2b. the same for a dialect whose second feed word is E
3. a thread lead is per revolution although the modal feed mode says per minute. M9 (WP9.5a): because the database says the F is the lead (rule 1), no longer because the code carries a pitch
3b. M9 (WP9.5a), changed: a pitch in force that the caller does not name may be a thread or a tap, and under a feed per minute the two are different numbers, so there is no class (it was feedPerRev)
3b2. M9: the same pitch nobody named under a feed per revolution is a feed per revolution either way
3b3. M9: the thread in force is named, and the database says its F is the lead, so a later F is a lead under a feed per minute too
3b4. M9: a tap is not a thread. The F of a mill G84 under G94 is the tap's feed per minute (the speed times the pitch), not a lead per revolution
3b5. M9: the same tap under G95 is a feed per revolution, the pitch itself
3b6. M9: a tapping mode in force (Fanuc G63, the modal pitch-feed mode of the Python tracker) is read as a tap: the feed is in the feed unit, here per minute
3b7. M9: Okuma G184 taps with a driven tool under G94; on a 1 um machine reading its F per revolution was 100 times off

params.label: Tapping feed, tied to the pitch

class.note: 3b8. M9: the F of Okuma G101 is a feed per minute whatever the feed mode, because the database says so
3b9. M9: and in the blocks after it, while G101 is the move in force
3b10. M9: a code in the block wins over the code in force
3b11. M9: a cycle parameter keeps its reading in the blocks that repeat the cycle in force
3c. a code that is a threading cycle in another G-code system says nothing: no class, no value
4. a rotary axis the profile lists is an angle

4b. the same letter on a profile that does not list it is an ordinary axis. M9 (WP9.5a): read on Klartext, because the mill lists its rotary axes now (it was the mill); M10 P10: on a profile of its own, because Klartext lists them now too
4d. M10 P10: Klartext lists its rotary axes A, B and C as angles (addresses.angular), so a simultaneous rotary move is seen as one
4c. M9 (WP9.5a): the Fanuc mill declares A, B and C angular, so C90000 is an angle and not 9 in
4d. M9: and so is a tilt axis A or B of a five-axis mill
5. the feed word by the modal feed unit: per minute
5b. the feed word by the modal feed unit: per revolution
5c. a feed while the feed unit is unknown has no class, so nothing converts it
5d. inverse time is not a length per time. M9 (WP9.5a), changed: it has a class of its own now, which no machine declares a reading for (it had none)
5e. a word that carries its own feed unit beats the modal one (Klartext FU)
5f. M9 (WP9.5a), changed: a feed per tooth has a class of its own, which no machine declares a reading for (it had none)
5f2. M9: a plain F under a per-tooth feed unit is a feed per tooth as well
5g. E is a feed per revolution on a dialect that says so
6. an axis is a length
6b. an incremental twin is a length as well
6c. an arc centre is a length
6d. R is a length wherever it stands, unless a cycle parameter says otherwise
7. a spindle speed has no number class at all
7b. a tool word has none either
7c. and neither has a G word
7d. an offset register is a number of a table, not a length
7e. a block number is not a value
a lower-case address is the same address
